name: SliceFleet for WooCommerce
author: baileysneppard

sections.description:
SliceFleet for WooCommerce gives your store instant, measured 3D print quotes. A customer uploads a model, the SliceFleet API slices it on a real slicing engine, and the quote is priced from the measured filament and print time at your own rates, then added to the cart as a normal WooCommerce line.

This is not a volume estimate. The result reports filament per slot, purge per slot, total filament, print time, and the model’s dimensions and volume, all measured by the engine.

You need a SliceFleet account and API key (a free plan is available) from slicefleet.com. The plugin itself is free; each quote uses one slice from your plan allowance.

What it includes:

  • Inline quote widget via shortcode or Gutenberg block: upload, 3D preview, per-part colours, painted multi-colour support, multiple parts in one quote
  • Four layout themes (Express, Standard, Guided, Studio) and appearance colours you can set
  • Your materials with per-gram rates and stocked colours, your printers with optional per-hour rates
  • Per-part quantity, per-item and order minimums, and a fallback message or form link for quotes that cannot be priced
  • Full order records in wp-admin: the model file, per-slot grams and purge, print time, chosen colours and options, and the price

Your API key stays on your server and is never sent to the customer’s browser. Prices are computed on your server from the measured result and your saved rates.

Files: STL and 3MF, up to your plan’s file limit. Painted multi-colour 3MF slices in full on the Bambu Studio engine and needs a paid SliceFleet plan.

External services

This plugin connects to the SliceFleet API to do its job. Slicing a customer’s model is the service: when a visitor requests a quote, your server sends the uploaded model file and the slicing settings for that quote to SliceFleet (slicefleet.com), which slices the file on a real engine and returns the measured result. The model file is deleted on SliceFleet’s side when the result is ready. The request carries the model and its slicing options, and your account is identified by your API key.

Where the host site enables it in the widget configuration, a “Slice the Benchy” sample button loads a reference model file from slicefleet.com into the visitor’s browser, so it can be quoted like any other model. Where the button is not enabled, that file is never requested.

SliceFleet terms of service: https://slicefleet.com/terms
SliceFleet privacy policy: https://slicefleet.com/privacy

Notes and limits

What the settings screen does not offer yet, because the capability behind it does not exist today (nothing here is faked or decorative):

  • Shopper controls for the rest of the extended slicing options (wall loops, shell layers, seam position, temperatures, infill pattern). Supports, brim and ironing have shopper on/off controls (2.9.0); the rest are multi-value or numeric settings and stay admin slice defaults.
  • A different default colour per plastic. The default colour is one name matched inside each plastic’s stocked colours.
  • Job-level API features in wp-admin (result callbacks, richer result detail, saved printer and filament configurations from your SliceFleet account). These are API-level features; the plugin does not expose them yet.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the slicefleet-for-woocommerce folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or upload the plugin zip under Plugins, Add New, Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate SliceFleet for WooCommerce in the Plugins screen. WooCommerce should be active for cart and checkout.
  3. Go to Settings, SliceFleet for WooCommerce. Paste your SliceFleet API key (it starts with sf_live_). The settings screen shows your plan usage once a key is saved.
  4. Add your materials with per-gram rates and stocked colours, your printers with any per-hour rates, your minimums, and your fallback message or form link. Save.
  5. Add the shortcode [slicefleet_quote] to a page, or insert the SliceFleet Quote block in the editor.
  6. Open the page and run a test quote with a small STL file to confirm your key and rates work. Place a test order and check the order in wp-admin: the SliceFleet box lists the file download and the per-slot breakdown.

Coming from SliceFleet Instant Quote (v1)? Your API key, materials, printer and minimum order are migrated to the new settings the first time the new plugin reads them. The old plugin’s settings are left untouched.
sections.faq:
Do I need a SliceFleet account?

Yes. The plugin calls the SliceFleet API with your account API key. Sign up at slicefleet.com. The free plan includes a monthly slice allowance, and each quote uses one slice. Failed slices never count.

Does the plugin cost anything?

The plugin is free. You pay only your SliceFleet plan, and plans start free. There is no separate licence key: your API key is the only credential, and your plan is checked by the API on every slice.

How is the price calculated?

Price equals total filament in grams (model plus purge) times your per-gram rate for the plastic the customer picked, plus print time in hours times the per-hour rate for the printer they picked. If a part comes out below your per-item minimum, the minimum applies to that part. Your order minimum is displayed with the quote total and never changes a line price by itself.

What is a failed slice?

If a slice comes back measuring under 0.01 g of total filament, the part did not really slice. It is excluded from the quote and cannot be added to the cart.

What files can customers upload?

STL and 3MF, up to your SliceFleet plan file limit (the free plan allows 50 MB per file, higher plans allow more). Painted multi-colour 3MF files slice in full on the Bambu Studio engine and need a paid SliceFleet plan. On other engines, coverage differs and the API returns a clear error rather than a partial result.

Where does the uploaded model go?

From the browser to your server, which keeps a copy in a protected uploads folder because you need the file to print the order. A copy also goes to SliceFleet for slicing and is deleted there when the result is ready. Direct web access to the stored copies is denied; shop admins download them from the order screen.

Can customers see my API key or change a price?

No. The key is stored in your WordPress options, used only in server side requests, and never printed, localized into scripts, or sent to the browser. Prices are computed on your server from the measured result and your saved rates, stored against the job, and add-to-cart always uses the stored price. Anything the browser sends claiming to be a price is ignored.

What happens when my slice allowance runs out?

The API returns a quota response and the customer sees your configured fallback (your message, or a link to your quote form), never a price. The real reason, allowance used up or an account billing stop, is visible to you in the plugin’s responses and your SliceFleet dashboard. Paid plans bill overage per slice instead of stopping at the allowance.

Which printers can I offer?

The printers the SliceFleet API slices today, picked from the supported list in settings (for example Bambu Lab A1, 0.4 mm nozzle, on the Bambu Studio engine), plus single-colour profiles on the OrcaSlicer and PrusaSlicer engines. The list is fetched live from the API, cached for a day, and falls back to a bundled snapshot, so it stays current without an update. Developers can enter a custom printer ID under a row’s Advanced toggle.
sections.changelog:
2.13.0

  • New: layout themes for the quote widget – Express (simple slice and quote), Standard (the essentials), Guided (a three-step upload, options and price flow) and Studio (the preview as the page, controls behind buttons around its edges). A theme is a starting point: picking one sets the shopper controls to the theme’s cluster, and every control stays individually editable afterwards. Existing installs keep their saved controls untouched.
  • The widget no longer ships its own outer frame: the styled container and header bar are gone, so your theme’s wrapper styles the quote.
  • Settings screen regrouped: the SliceFleet API key and Default slicing engine section leads, then the layout group (layout theme, appearance and the quote settings – details layout and both minimums), shopper controls, materials, printers, slicing defaults, advanced slicing defaults, and the “When quote cannot be priced” fallback last. The Presentation, Sample button and Hide upload trigger settings and the whole “Before model is uploaded” section are removed; any values saved for them are ignored, and every remaining setting keeps its name and meaning.

2.12.0

  • “Plastics” are now called “Materials” across the settings page, the setup wizard and the shopper widget. Nothing under the hood moved: the stored keys, payload keys and option names are unchanged, and existing settings carry over untouched.
  • Printers, materials, material filament profiles and slice-default filament profiles are now picked from searchable dropdowns fed by the SliceFleet capabilities list (live fetch on the settings screen, a 24-hour cache, and a bundled snapshot as the last resort, plus a “Refresh from SliceFleet” button). Saving a value the list does not carry is rejected with an error naming it, unless the row is marked custom under its Advanced toggle – the developer escape hatches (custom printer IDs with engine overrides, custom material names) are kept, hidden behind Advanced.
  • A material can map to a real filament profile: for an unpainted, single-colour part that profile is sent to the slicer in slot 1, over the slice-default profiles. Painted parts are unchanged – the file’s own filaments stay, and the material prices every slot. An unmapped material stays price-and-preview only, exactly as before.
  • Colour picks never start a new slice: plain and painted-slot picks are order and display data, per-colour price modifiers reprice from the stored slice result, and slot picks no longer merge slots into one filament in the slice. Reslices happen on file, printer, material and slice-settings changes only.
  • New opt-in shop setting, off by default: “Auto-map painted colours to stocked colours” pre-matches a painted part’s slots to the nearest stocked colour of its material when the part loads.
  • Slice-default filament profiles are per-slot dropdowns (the stored list format is unchanged), the infill pattern suggests the common patterns while free text still passes to the engine as-is, and defaults an engine does not apply are greyed with a “Not applied by” note. The setup wizard now prefills all four Bambu A1 nozzle sizes.

2.11.1

  • Directory build: the wordpress.org package omits the self-hosted updater, because the directory provides updates itself and does not permit plugin updaters. The direct download from slicefleet.com keeps the self-hosted updater; the plugin loads it only when the file is present, so the two builds behave identically in every other way.
  • Added the missing translators comments to the placeholder strings in the setup flow.

2.11.0

  • Maintenance: every plugin identifier now carries one distinct prefix, slicfowo_ (functions, classes, constants, options, transients, AJAX actions, hooks and the jobs table), replacing the short sfw_ prefix. Existing installs migrate automatically on upgrade: settings, onboarding state and the product pointer are copied to the new option names and verified before the old names are removed, and the jobs table is renamed (or merged, when both exist) with its records intact. Order records keep their history – new orders write slicfowo item meta and the pre-2.11 sfw meta stays readable as a fallback. Short-lived transients under the old prefix simply lapse. The [slicefleet_quote] shortcode, the block and the text domain are unchanged.
  • The plugin header now declares its WooCommerce dependency (Requires Plugins: woocommerce), the readme short description fits the directory limit, the bundled Three.js viewer library is updated to the current stable release, and the plugin no longer calls load_plugin_textdomain() (WordPress loads directory translations itself).

2.10.0

  • New: self-hosted updates. Installs from the slicefleet.com direct download now check a signed-checksum update manifest on slicefleet.com and offer updates through the normal WordPress plugins screen. The package checksum is verified before anything installs. If a site is managed through wordpress.org instead, wordpress.org updates win and the self-hosted checker stays out of the way.
  • New: a three step setup flow on activation (Settings – SliceFleet Setup): paste your API key with a live connection test, confirm the prefilled plastics and printers, then place the quote widget with the block or the [slicefleet_quote] shortcode. It is dismissible, resumable, never blocks wp-admin, and skips itself when an API key is already saved.

2.9.0

  • New: Gutenberg block. The SliceFleet Quote block embeds the quote in the block editor with a clear placeholder; on the front end it renders through the same code path as the [slicefleet_quote] shortcode – same mount, same widget, no second rendering logic.
  • New: per-instance overrides. The shortcode and the block can each override the presentation and the appearance (a preset, or the Custom preset with its own primary/accent pair) for that embed only: [slicefleet_quote presentation=”simple” theme=”custom” primary=”#112233″ accent=”#445566″]. Attributes are sanitized exactly like the corresponding settings and never mutate the saved settings.
  • New: shopper controls for supports, brim and ironing. Three new “Show in the quote” toggles (off by default) add on/off pill controls for those options to the quote panel. A part starts from the shop’s slice defaults and a shopper pick replaces the default for that option, exactly like layer height and infill: supports on sends normal supports, brim on sends the shop’s brim width (5 mm when unset) and off sends 0, ironing sends its boolean. The picks ride in the slice options and are stored on the order record.
  • New: per-part quantity. Each part card gains a quantity stepper (1 to 99). The quantity multiplies the part’s material and time price and its shipping weight: the part card shows the line total, the quote details carry the unit price, the quantity and the line total, the quote total sums the lines, the cart line carries the quantity as its WooCommerce quantity (so the line total and weight-based shipping scale with it), and the order line records the quantity and the line total. Everything reconciles to the cent. The demo bridge prices quantity identically (per-unit price times the sanitized quantity).

2.8.5

  • Critical fix: file uploads failed with a PHP error on every real upload since 2.8.3. The upload handler passed its file array inline to wp_handle_upload(), whose first argument is by reference; the array is now passed as a variable, as the API requires. Uploads, slicing and quoting work again. (The automated tests only exercised the non-upload fallback path, which is why this shipped; a source-level regression check now covers it.)

2.8.4

  • Per-colour price modifiers: every stocked colour now carries an additive per-gram price modifier (default 0, editable beside the colour in the plastics settings; it can be negative). A single-colour part prices at (plastic rate + the picked colour’s modifier) times its measured total filament. A painted part prices per slot: each slot’s measured grams including its flushed share, at the plastic rate plus the modifier of the stocked colour mapped to that slot, computed from the slicing API’s returned per-filament grams and flushed amounts only. The quote breakdown shows the applied rate (per slot on painted parts), so the numbers reconcile exactly.
  • Custom theme preset: the Appearance preset list gains Custom. Your own primary/accent pair is saved persistently as its own setting: editing either colour updates the pair, choosing a named preset applies the preset without touching the pair, and choosing Custom re-applies the pair. Settings stored by earlier versions keep resolving exactly as they did until the next save.
  • Fresh-install stocked colours trimmed to the common sets: PLA starts with 8 colours, PETG with 5, and ASA is now a third prefilled plastic with 5. Existing stores keep their saved colours untouched – this changes only the starting point for new installs.

2.8.3

  • Sample Benchy: on hosts whose slicing endpoint keeps its own copy of the reference file (the SliceFleet demo), “Slice the Benchy” now submits by reference – the quote no longer waits for the sample file to download and is not followed by an upload of the same 11 MB, so it prices in seconds even on a slow connection. The sample file still loads in parallel for the 3D preview. On every other host the button behaves exactly as before, and ordinary file uploads are unchanged everywhere.

2.8.2

  • Pre-upload results placeholder: the totals-footer skeleton’s total spot no longer imitates the price sentence with dashes. It now shows a short generic status line, “Waiting for your model”, in the same style as the widget’s slicing status lines. The greyed-out Add to Cart button is unchanged, the skeleton keeps the real footer’s exact footprint, and the results area set to appear only after an upload still renders nothing before one.

2.8.1

  • Pre-upload results placeholder: the totals-footer skeleton no longer draws grey bars. The total spot now shows the sentence itself in muted text with dashes where the numbers will land (“Across — parts, total $–“), and the button spot is the Add to Cart button greyed out, its label showing, disabled until a quote prices it. The skeleton keeps the real footer’s exact footprint, so the quote still lands with no layout shift, and the results area set to appear only after an upload still renders nothing before one.

2.8.0

  • Fix: the 3D preview now centres the model and keeps it fully in frame at every size, phones included. On high-resolution screens the preview canvas could lay out larger than its viewer, pushing the centred render out of the visible corner; the canvas now fills its viewer in layout terms, and the camera fit uses the viewer’s actual shape (the narrower of the vertical and horizontal views) and re-fits whenever the viewer changes size.
  • Settings screen: reorganized for a quicker read. Every description is now a short phrase or gone. The five shopper-control toggles are one checklist, the pre-upload panel and per-area choices sit in one compact group with short labels, and the slicing defaults live under one collapsed “Advanced slicing defaults” heading. Nothing functional changed: every setting keeps its name, its values and its meaning, and saved settings work exactly as before.

2.7.7

  • Pre-upload results placeholder: the results area no longer shows a “No model yet” sentence in a dashed box before an upload. In its placeholder mode it now shows a skeleton of the totals footer – a muted bar where the total will sit and a muted block the Add to Cart button’s own size, in a strip matching the footer’s own spacing – so the real footer lands in exactly the space the skeleton held and the page barely shifts when a quote arrives. Set the results area to appear only after an upload and nothing renders there before one, as before.

2.7.6

  • Layout: the batch progress strip (“Slicing part X of Y”) no longer renders at the very bottom of the panel. It now sits directly below the 3D preview in the left column, between the preview and the part cards, so the slicing progress reads next to the model it belongs to; in the stacked single-column layout it follows the same position under the preview. The strip itself, its wording and its timing are unchanged, and single-part slices behave exactly as before.

2.7.4

  • Appearance themes: the preset list is now Generic, Ember, Lagoon, Forest and Berry. Lagoon is a new deep teal-and-coral pair (primary #0B4F5C, accent #FF8A5B) in the third slot, replacing the retired preset. A store whose saved appearance named the retired preset falls back to the Generic default; any custom colours it set are kept as overrides.

2.7.3

  • Fix: spacing below the quote details in the results band. The details block (Grid and Stack layouts) now carries the grid’s own 8px gap below itself, so its last row no longer sits flush against the across-parts total and Add to Cart footer that follow it. The Popover layout is unchanged – its panel already carries the spacing.

2.7.2

  • Appearance themes: the preset list is now Generic, Ember, Lagoon, Forest and Berry. Ember is a new warm pair (primary #7C2D12, accent #E8A33D) in the second slot. A store whose saved appearance named the retired preset falls back to the Generic default; any custom colours it set are kept as overrides.

2.7.1

  • Runtime reconfiguration: a running widget can now be reconfigured in place through updateSettings() on the instance (kept on its mount element as sfwWidget). The new settings are normalized like the boot settings and re-rendered live: appearance colours swap as CSS variables, the entry zone rebuilds for the presentation, sample-button and upload-trigger settings, the details re-render from the part’s existing result in the newly chosen layout, and the empty state follows the pre-upload settings. The quote itself never resets – parts, results, prices, shopper selections, the preview and in-flight slices are untouched, and a layout switch never auto-opens the details popover (that stays a fresh-slice behaviour). Shopper defaults changed at runtime seed only parts that do not exist yet; a pre-upload draft the shopper has already changed keeps their picks.

2.7.0

  • Popover quote details: the “Quote details layout” setting gains a third option, Popover. The active part’s details render in a panel anchored to the top-left corner of the preview (opposite the colour selector), opened from a round icon button in that corner. The panel opens on its own when a slice finishes, clicking the preview fades it away and brings the icon back, and switching parts swaps the open panel’s contents. The quote total and Add to Cart stay in the results band.
  • Part cards moved under the preview: the parts list (each card with its name, status and per-part price) now renders directly below the 3D preview in the left column instead of inside the full-width results band, which keeps only the quote details (Grid and Stack layouts), the notes, the total and Add to Cart.
  • Add-part tile: the “+ Add another file” button is replaced by a dashed-outline tile the size of a part card, sitting beside the parts in their grid; clicking it opens the file picker for another part.
  • Details order: in every layout the model’s dimensions now render in among the other measured stats, and the part’s price is simply the last item – an ordinary cell or row like the rest, no longer a distinct full-width row.
  • Clickable empty preview: before a model is chosen, clicking the empty preview area opens the file picker, and its text says so, in every presentation.
  • New setting, “Hide the upload trigger” (off by default): renders no upload control of the plugin’s own – no drop zone, no Choose a file button, and the “Slice the Benchy” sample button does not render either. The quote panel shows upfront and the clickable empty preview is the only upload path. The Custom presentation’s own trigger element is unaffected.

2.6.0

  • Results band layout: at wide panel widths the pricing results – the part cards with their per-part prices, the quote details, the total and the Add to Cart button – now span the full width of the panel in a band below the viewer and settings columns, instead of sitting in the left column under the viewer. The viewer and settings keep their two columns above it.
  • Quote details layout setting: a part’s quote details (weights, purge, costs, print time, dimensions) render as a compact grid of label-and-value cells by default, stepping from four columns on ultrawide panels down to two on phones, with the part price kept as a distinct full-width row. A new “Quote details layout” setting in the plugin’s Appearance section switches the details back to the previous single-column stacked list if you prefer it.

2.5.5

  • Tier card layout in the split view: the plastic and printer tier cards no longer stack one per row in the settings rail – they flow in condensed rows, as many across as fit above a readable card width, at every split width. The cards in a row share the row evenly, so a single card left on the last row spans the full width instead of sitting as a narrow orphan. Works for any number of plastics and printers a shop configures.

2.5.4

  • Mobile tier cards: the plastic and printer tier cards no longer stack one per row at small widths – they hold their side-by-side row, and the plastic card’s description drops its ” in stock” suffix at those widths so the plastic name and colour count fit the narrower cards. The full text returns at larger widths.

2.5.3

  • Print settings layout: each pill group (layer height, infill) now puts its title in a compact label column beside an even grid of equal-width pills, instead of the title taking its own line and the pills wrapping unevenly – the column count at each layout width divides the option count, so no group ends with a lone pill.

2.5.2

  • Ultrawide layout: the quote panel no longer stops at a width ceiling, and a new layout tier at 1900px of embed width widens the settings rail to 600px and groups its tier cards and print-setting rows into two-across sub-columns, so on ultrawide embeds both columns fill the full width with the settings still compact and grouped.

2.5.1

  • Fix: the “Slice the Benchy” sample button is a true outline button – no background colour in any state (default, hover, focus, active), just the primary-colour border and text, so it reads quieter than the solid upload button beside it.

2.5.0

  • New: Appearance themes. The default theme is now Generic, a neutral pair (#1F2937 and #D97706) chosen to sit inside an arbitrary shop’s branding; the preset list is Generic, Ember, Lagoon, Forest and Berry. Custom primary and accent colours still override the preset per colour, and colours stored before themes existed are kept as overrides.
  • New: Pre-upload visibility settings. The panel can show upfront before any upload (settings live, viewer and results as placeholders – the default), stay hidden until a model is uploaded, and each area (viewer, settings, results) can individually show as a placeholder upfront or appear only after an upload. Choices made on the upfront draft seed the first part.
  • New: a “Slice the Benchy” sample button setting (on by default). When on, an outline button beside the upload control loads the reference Benchy through the normal quote flow; when off, no button renders. In the Custom presentation the plugin renders no entry controls, so no sample button appears there either.

2.4.0

  • The quote panel no longer carries window chrome: the header shows just the selected model’s file name (no thumbnail, no minimize or close buttons), there is no collapse and no collapsed “open your quote” line. The panel is page content and stays on the page; removing a part stays on the part card.
  • New: Custom presentation. The plugin renders no trigger of its own and binds its file picker to an element you supply – any element with the attribute data-slicefleet-trigger, or the element whose id you pass as the shortcode’s trigger_id attribute. Whether the quote sits in a dialog is your choice: your trigger can live in your own dialog, drawer or menu. If no trigger element exists, the simple upload button renders instead and a warning is logged to the browser console.
  • Layout: at 900px of embed width and up, the quote splits into two columns – the 3D viewer on the left with the quoted results (part cards, price lines, totals, Add to Cart) directly under it, and all settings (colour, plastic, printer, print settings) in the right rail, so a long settings list never pushes the results away from the model. The split sizes down between 900px and 1099px instead of breaking, and on very wide embeds (1500px and up) the panel and viewer keep growing while the settings rail stays at its organized width. Below 900px the sections stack in reading order: viewer, settings, results.
  • Setting pills and slot pills are single units that never wrap mid-control, and tier cards stack one per row inside the settings rail.

2.3.0

  • The quote experience now renders inline on the page – the viewer, per-part settings and results appear in the page flow where the shortcode sits. There is no modal dialog, no backdrop and no floating dock; collapsing the panel leaves the quote as a line with Open and Cancel actions.
  • New: Presentation setting – Designed (the branded drop zone) or Simple (a single upload button). Choosing a file renders the full quote inline in both modes.
  • New: Shopper controls – show or hide the plastic picker, the printer picker, the colour picker, and the layer height and infill settings, each independently.
  • New: Shopper defaults – the plastic, printer, layer height, infill and colour every new part starts with.
  • New: Slice defaults – wall loops, shell layers, supports, seam position, ironing, infill pattern, temperatures and filament profiles, sent with every slice.
  • New: a per-printer engine override, so different printer profiles can slice on different engines.
  • A fresh install now comes prefilled with a working store skeleton (PLA and PETG with stocked colours, one printer, every shopper control on) so the plugin quotes out of the box once an API key is saved.

2.2.0

  • New: Appearance settings – the quote dialog’s primary and accent colours are now shop settings (defaults #154a87 and #E5B700), applied to the dialog as CSS custom properties with derived shades and tints following the chosen colours.
  • New: Display settings – choose whether the quote dialog shows the Layer height and Infill print settings; turn both off and the Print settings section is hidden entirely.
  • The dialog layout is now responsive to the width of its mount (CSS container queries): a wide two-column layout with a tall viewer at 1100px and up, the standard dialog between 641px and 1099px, and stacked narrow and phone layouts at 640px and 420px.

2.1.1

  • Fix: the native file input no longer shows inside the drop area on themes that style input elements – it is visually hidden (sr-only pattern) while remaining the real input behind the Choose a file button and drag-and-drop.

2.0.0

  • Full WooCommerce plugin. Quote experience with preview and per-part colour selection, painted multi-colour support with per-slot grams and purge, server-computed pricing from your plastics and printers, cart lines on a managed hidden product with sliced weight for shipping, and full order records with a protected model file download.
  • Settings migrated automatically from SliceFleet Instant Quote (v1) when present.

This plugin connects to the SliceFleet API to do its job. Slicing a customer’s model is the service: when a visitor requests a quote, your server sends the uploaded model file and the slicing settings for that quote to SliceFleet (slicefleet.com), which slices the file on a real engine and returns the measured result. The model file is deleted on SliceFleet’s side when the result is ready. The request carries the model and its slicing options, and your account is identified by your API key.

Where the host site enables it in the widget configuration, a “Slice the Benchy” sample button loads a reference model file from slicefleet.com into the visitor’s browser, so it can be quoted like any other model. Where the button is not enabled, that file is never requested.

SliceFleet terms of service: https://slicefleet.com/terms
SliceFleet privacy policy: https://slicefleet.com/privacy

Notes and limits

What the settings screen does not offer yet, because the capability behind it does not exist today (nothing here is faked or decorative):

  • Shopper controls for the rest of the extended slicing options (wall loops, shell layers, seam position, temperatures, infill pattern). Supports, brim and ironing have shopper on/off controls (2.9.0); the rest are multi-value or numeric settings and stay admin slice defaults.
  • A different default colour per plastic. The default colour is one name matched inside each plastic’s stocked colours.
  • Job-level API features in wp-admin (result callbacks, richer result detail, saved printer and filament configurations from your SliceFleet account). These are API-level features; the plugin does not expose them yet.
